ask: My costs have gone up a lot this year and I have my own mortgage to cover, so I need £1,450 a month from the renewal. Can you confirm that is OK?
text:
Dear Mr Hadley,

Thank you for letting us know, and I'm sorry to hear your costs have gone up so much this year.

We would very much like to renew for another year. We've been happy here for three years. In that time we've paid the rent in full and on time every month, and we've looked after the property as if it were our own.

However, £1,450 would be a rise of £200 a month, about 16%, and that is more than we can take on. We'd like to ask if you would keep the rent at £1,250 for the coming year. Reliable long-term tenants mean no empty months, no letting fees and no risk with someone new, and we hope that counts for something when you weigh up your costs.

We're happy to talk this through and would like to agree something that works for both of us.

Kind regards

ask: We are first-time buyers and £378,000 is the very top of our mortgage offer. We love the house. Will you accept it?
text:
Hi,

Thank you for your offer. We're really glad you love the house.

We can't accept £378,000, but we can meet you at £385,000. That's the lowest we can go. The asking price was £415,000, so it's a big reduction, and it reflects the new kitchen we put in in 2023 and the south-facing garden.

We've already bought our next home, so there's no onward chain on our side. That means we can move as fast as you and your mortgage lender can.

We know £385,000 is more than your current mortgage offer. Some buyers close a gap like this by asking their lender or a broker whether they can borrow a little more, or by adding a bit more to their deposit. If you can get to £385,000, we'd be happy to agree the sale with you and take the house off the market.

Please let us know what you think.

Best wishes

ask: With the new features and our own cost rises, the renewal comes to £32,500 a year. Shall I send the order form?
text:
Hi Dana,

Thanks for sending this through. Please hold off on the order form for now.

£32,500 would be a rise of more than 35% on the £24,000 we pay now. That's well beyond what we can justify internally for a renewal. For our 85 users, it takes the cost per user from about £282 to about £382 a year, and we haven't seen a case for that change yet.

To help us look at it properly, could you send:

We'd like to keep working with Ledgerly. For a 12-month renewal, we'd be looking at something closer to £26,000 a year. We're also open to a longer commitment if the pricing reflects that.

With the contract ending on 30 June, I'd like to get this settled in good time. Would a call in the next couple of weeks work for you?

Best regards
